text:
alex: Heads-up — since the scheduler qlen admission tweak rolled last night, we're seeing a long tail on r-llama2-13b-gen in dedicated-us-west. p99 jumped from ~180ms to ~2.7s around 03:12 UTC. Not all hosts, looks like a subset.
maya: ugh. saw an alert. is this the qlen->weight change in the admission controller? :thinking_face:
alex: yeah that one. only change was shifting weight from `size_estimate` to `queue_length` to prioritize short-queue nodes. might be overfavoring nodes with small KV caches?

cheng: grabbing profiles now. initial hunch: continuous-batcher is creating many tiny microbatches for long-seq requests which then hit a kernel path that isn't optimized for small batch counts — kernel selector flips to fallback path under 4-way packing.

ops-bot: incident-created: INC-219876 - r-llama2 tail latency spike (assigned: cheng) :rotating_light:

cheng: quick sampling of the worker that showed spike:
```
# from perf sampling
main_loop           52.3%  batcher::attempt_pack
kernel_selector      21.1%  pick_fallback_path_if_packing_low
kv_cache             10.2%  eviction_check
others                6.4%  syscall
```
Seems like `pick_fallback_path_if_packing_low` is hot when microbatch size < 4.

maya: does the admission change bias small microbatch creation? I thought we cap min_batch=2 but maybe continuous-batcher internal thresholds misread queue_length.
alex: exactly — the qlen weight causes some hosts to accept many single-request admissions because they report near-zero queue length, but those requests are long sequences (1k+ tokens) so they don't pack well.
sarah: KV cache churn note — those hosts with p99s also show higher kv eviction rates. probable cause: single-request long seqs thrash KV and evict prefixes that would have helped packing later.

cheng: pasted a quick small repro load on a staging replica:
```
# simulate long-seq mix
wrk -c50 -t4 --script longseq.lua http://staging-replica.local/gen
# observe microbatch sizes
cat /proc/batcher/stats | jq '.microbatch_histogram'
```
Output: most microbatches are size=1, 2% size>=4.

maya: ok that matches. two levers: 1) revert qlen weight tweak, 2) change admission policy to include `estimated_seq_len` signal so hosts avoid taking long-seq singletons when packing low.
alex: can we do a fast mitigation? maybe bump `min_packing_threshold` to 4 so kernel selector doesn't pick fallback slow path.
cheng: quick patch ready — set `min_pack_for_fast_kernel=4` and add guard to continuous-batcher to delay admitting if estimated_seq_len>800 and current_pack<2. I can roll to canary now.

ops-bot: deploy-started: canary/adaptive-batcher-patch (by cheng)

cheng: rolling to 10% canary in us-west 1. monitoring p99.

maya: also adding kv_cache retention tweak — increase max_prefix_entries on canary hosts by 20% to reduce eviction while we test.
alex: nice. thank you. if canary looks good for 10m, promote and then follow-up with admission change that uses `estimated_seq_len` permanently.

cheng: canary results after 6m: p99 on canary dropped to 220ms, non-canary still 2.5s. microbatch histogram now: size>=4 ~45% on canary.

maya: looks safe. promoting.

ops-bot: deploy-complete: rollout/adaptive-batcher-patch -> 100% (by cheng)

alex: post-rollout checks: p50/p95 stable, p99 trending back to baseline. opening a follow-up PR to add telemetry for `estimated_seq_len` to admission decisions and a unit test for packing thresholds.

sarah: note for postmortem: root cause = admission weighting change combined with distribution shift (more long-seq traffic on a subset) -> created many un-packable singletons -> kernel selector fallback + kv thrash -> tail latency. Mitigation: canary patch + kv retention bump. Next: formalize admission signals.

cheng: I'll write runbook steps for future — include quick checks: `microbatch_histogram`, `kv_eviction_rate`, `kernel_fallback_hits`. saving logs to /var/lib/rt/INC-219876.

maya: thanks everyone. filing incident summary and linking to PRs. :thumbsup:
